text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Prime Minister Hariri says the U.S. decision to keep the travel ban on Lebanon is not justified.

-Major-General Levine, Israel's northern commander, was at the Braachit post on the edge of Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone when it came under Hizbollah guerrilla attack. Israel retaliated by targeting guerrilla positions.
-Hariri will meet French President Chirac in Paris on Saturday.
-Seven members of parliament proposed a draft law to uncover illegal wealth.
-Commercial banks deposits reached 29,358 billion Lebanese pounds in the first ten months of 1996, the Banks Association said.
-Lebanon's public debt reached 18,244 billion Lebanese pounds at the end of October 1996, the Banks Association said.

-Palestinian refugees in Burj Ashamali refugee camp in the coastal city of Tyre will go on a one-day strike today to protest against the "unfair" social policy of the U.N. Relief and Works Agency for Palestinian refugees in the Near East .
